chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha' who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ziyad! Beware of disputes, for they beget doubt, bring down one's deeds, and ruin the one who engages in them; and perhaps he may say something and not be forgiven for it.

Indeed, in the past there were a people who abandoned the knowledge they were entrusted with and sought knowledge they were relieved of, until their discourse reached [the subject of] God and they became confused — to the extent that the man would be called from in front of him and he would answer from behind him, and he would be called from behind him and he would answer from in front of him.
And in another report: 'until they wandered in the earth.'

key_terms.الخصومات: Theological disputes, contentious debates, polemical arguments
key_terms.الشك: Doubt, uncertainty in matters of faith
key_terms.تَحَيَّرُوا: They became bewildered, confused, lost direction
key_terms.كُفُوهُ: Relieved of it, spared from it (knowledge beyond their station)
key_terms.وُكِّلُوا بِهِ: Entrusted with it, assigned/obligated to it (knowledge proper to their station)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about engaging in theological disputes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) warns his companion Ziyad against engaging in theological disputes (khusuma) about matters beyond human ken, particularly speculative arguments about the divine nature. The Imam uses vivid imagery of mental disorientation — a man who cannot tell front from back — to describe how such overreaching intellectual hubris destroys both faith and moral action. Historically, this teaching was directed at those who were attracted to the Mu'tazilite and early kalam (speculative theology) circles, which were active in the 2nd century AH; the Imams consistently taught that the divine essence (kayfiyya, the 'how') is beyond human comprehension.
word_analysis: their companion/the one who engages in them
